title: I’ve been building AI-powered tools for my investing workflow — would love feedback and ideas
author: ybant1990
selftext:
Over the past few months, I’ve been experimenting with Claude AI to build tools that make my investing and trading process more systematic.

Two tools I’ve built so far:

📊 **Watchlist Tracker:** [https://claude.ai/artifact/MeD7ns7AwB7r7PezrjnWfq](https://claude.ai/artifact/MeD7ns7AwB7r7PezrjnWfq)

📓 **Trade Journal:** [https://claude.ai/artifact/KhPtQ25beVPqcpT2m4wj1m](https://claude.ai/artifact/KhPtQ25beVPqcpT2m4wj1m)

I’m also exploring investment frameworks, market analysis dashboards, and other tools to simplify research and decision-making.

I share some of my experiments and learnings on my YouTube channel, **yashbuildswithai**: [https://www.youtube.com/@YashbuildswithAI](https://www.youtube.com/@YashbuildswithAI)

To be clear, the purpose of this post isn't to promote my channel. I want to connect with like-minded people interested in AI and investing, exchange ideas, get honest feedback, and collaborate on building tools that solve real problems for the investing community.

I'd love to know:

* What features would you add to the watchlist tracker or trade journal?
* What repetitive investing or trading tasks would you like AI to simplify?
* Is anyone else experimenting with building financial tools using AI?

These are works in progress, and I'm keen to learn from the community and build better tools together. Happy to exchange ideas!

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: I’d connect the Watchlist Tracker to the Trade Journal through an immutable thesis history. When someone adds a ticker with the M10 timeframe, entry price, star rating, and “Why this setup?” note shown in the screenshot, save that original record with a timestamp. Later edits should create versions rather than overwrite it, and a trade should link back to the exact version that prompted entry. Since the data is browser-only with backup/restore, include schema versioning and stable IDs in the export so restores do not break those links. That would make the tools useful for reviewing whether a thesis changed before or after the outcome was known.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: for the journal I'd add a field for why you took the trade, filled in before the exit, so later you can grade the reason and not just the result. I built the testing half myself: Quantradin replays a written rule over US stock history with no peeking ahead, free on fake money. quantradin.com. does the watchlist tracker trigger anything yet, or is it tracking only?

comments.author: itlogicpartnersllc
comments.body: a useful addition would be an ai post trade review that compares your original thesis with what actually happened it could flag recurring mistakes without pretending to predict the market..

replies.author: ybant1990
replies.body: Makes sense I will also try to link it with Kite API and see if it works

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good use of AI for the boring parts. For the trade journal, the feature I'd add first is a field for the reason and the expected outcome before each trade, then a review that compares expected with actual, grouped by setup and by whether you followed your own rules. For the watchlist, an alert when a name hits a level you set in advance saves the most time. Full disclosure, I work at Cymetica, and one tool you might find useful for your workflow is Backtest Labs, where you can test a rule against history with fees included before it goes into your journal as a setup.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
For a prop-oriented journal, I’d add “risk budget at entry” next to the thesis: remaining daily loss allowance, distance to the applicable drawdown threshold, open exposure and the rule version. Then the review can distinguish a valid setup taken too large from a bad signal. It’s also useful to preserve rejected or deliberately skipped entries, rather than only executed trades.



We’re QATS. If you’d like to try that as a separate perpetuals-prop integration, our Trading API exposes account/risk state, orders, executions and positions: [https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/](https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/) . It isn’t a stock broker connection or an existing integration with your tools. Evaluations and initial funded accounts are simulated; server-side plan limits still apply.
